evidence: number-notnull.validator.ts: NumberNotNullValidator.addRules() checks value === null/undefined, Number.isNaN (skipped when allowNaN is set) and !Number.isFinite (skipped when allowInfinity is set).

number-positive.validator.ts: NumberPositiveValidator.addRules() repeats the null/undefined check, rejects NaN with no allowNaN option, and rejects any non-finite value with no allowInfinity option. NumberPositiveValidationOptions has neither flag.

number.valueobject.ts: NumberValueObject.addValidators() adds NumberNotNullValidator({allowNaN, allowInfinity}) and also NumberPositiveValidator when requirePositive is true (the default via DEFAULT_NUMBER_OPTIONS). The second validator then rejects values the first was told to allow.

string.valueobject.ts: StringMaxLengthValidator.addRules() returns early on null with the comment 'Null/undefined is StringNotNullOrEmptyValidator's rule to report'. The number validators do not follow this convention.

number.valueobject.ts DEFAULT_NUMBER_OPTIONS (allowNaN:false, allowInfinity:false, epsilon:0, allowZero:false) are repeated as hard-coded defaults in the NumberNotNullValidator and NumberPositiveValidator constructors.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module covers one concern: primitive value objects (Id, Number, String) built on DddValueObject, with their AbstractRuleValidator rules. It fails the rubric because the number-validity rule (not null, not NaN, finite) is written twice, and the two copies disagree.

NumberNotNullValidator can be configured with allowNaN and allowInfinity. NumberPositiveValidator repeats the same null, NaN and finite checks but has no way to relax them. NumberValueObject.addValidators registers both validators, and positivity is on by default (requirePositive: true). So NumberValueObject.create(NaN, { allowNaN: true }) and create(Infinity, { allowInfinity: true }) are still rejected, and a NaN value reports 'cannot be NaN' twice.

The string validators avoid this: StringMaxLengthValidator explicitly leaves null reporting to StringNotNullOrEmptyValidator. The number validators do not follow that convention.

The default flags are also defined twice: DEFAULT_NUMBER_OPTIONS in number.valueobject.ts and the hard-coded defaults in each number validator's constructor.

IdValueObject checks the UUID format in both assertUuid and UuidFormatValidator. Both call the same validateUuid, and the code documents why there are two checks (one throws immediately, the other keeps isValid accurate on later re-validation), so I do not count it as a violation.

violations.message: NumberPositiveValidator.addRules() repeats NumberNotNullValidator's null, NaN and finite checks without its allowNaN/allowInfinity options. The same rule therefore exists in two places with different behaviour.

NumberValueObject.addValidators() registers NumberNotNullValidator (with allowNaN/allowInfinity) and NumberPositiveValidator, which repeats and overrides those checks. With the default requirePositive: true, the documented allowNaN/allowInfinity options have no effect, and NaN produces duplicate broken rules. The validators' defaults also repeat DEFAULT_NUMBER_OPTIONS.
